44-ACC0000010.title: Accountant, Certified Public
44-ACC0000010.description: Prepares, analyzes and verifies financial reports. Keeps, prepares and reviews client records, which detail all financial transactions. May choose to concentrate on one area of practice such as auditing, taxation or management services.
44-ACC0000010.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Board of Accountancy

00-78.title: Enrolled Actuary
00-78.description: Enrolled Actuaries meet experience requirements and pass an examination. EAs are experts on the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). The EA designation is awarded by the Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries, located at the Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury. Renewal every 3 years requires continuing actuarial education and other professional development activities. For detailed information, see http://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-utl/20cfr901.pdf or http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/actuaries/index.html.
00-78.agency: U.S. Department of the Treasury · Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries

44-ENG0000410.title: Engineer, Professional
44-ENG0000410.description: Engages in the practical application of physical laws and principles of engineering for the development and utilization of machines, materials, instruments, processes, and services. Include engineers in research, development, production, technical services, and other positions which require knowledge normally obtained through completion of a 4-year engineering college program. Exclude persons trained in engineering but currently working in positions that do not require engineering training. Exclude sales engineers.
44-ENG0000410.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · State Board of Registration for Professional Engineers

00-18.title: Air Traffic Control Tower Operator
00-18.description: Requirements to obtain an Air Traffic Control Tower Operator certificate include passing a written test. Besides the basic certificate, to act at any operating position, the individual must pass a practical test on control tower equipment and its use. To obtain a facility rating, the individual must have at least six months experience and pass another practical test. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended or revoked, although the individual must maintain current experience to work under the certificate. Detailed information can be found at web sites:http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, http://www.natca.org/assets/Documents/mediacenter/controller_brochure.pdf, http://www2.faa.gov/careers/employment/atc.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.31-65.50.

00-12.title: Aircraft Mechanic - A & P
00-12.description: Aircraft mechanics are certified by the FAA with either an airframe (A) or powerplant (P) rating. Initial ratings require either completion of FAA Approved Aviation Maintenance Technician School or 18 months of work experience. Applicants must pass written, oral and practical exams. Thirty months of work experience is required for a combined Airframe & Powerplant (A & P) certificate. To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an A & P certificate for at least 3 years. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked, but requires currency of experience or refresher training. For further information, go the web site of the Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS): http://umet-vets.dol.gov/airframe-mechanic.htm, http://www1.faa.gov/AVR/afs/mechanics.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.71-65.95.

00-16.title: Aircraft Repairer
00-16.description: To be eligible for a repairman certificate, a person must have the qualifications needed on the job. These qualifications may be obtained through 18 months of work experience or completion of formal training. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www2.faa.gov/education/rlib/career.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.101-65.105.

00-02.title: Airline Transport Pilot
00-02.description: To become certified (licensed) as an Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), an individual must have a Commercial Pilot certificate or equivalent with an instrument rating for airplane, helicopter, or powered-lift (glider). Air flight training and ground school as well as flight experience are requirements. They also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. They must pass a written test and a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.151-61.167.

00-08.title: Commercial Pilot
00-08.description: All pilots who are paid to transport passengers or cargo must have a Commercial Pilot's license with an instrument rating issued by the FAA. To qualify for this license, the applicant must be at least 18 years old and have at least 250 hours of flight experience. The time can be reduced through participation in certain flight school curricula approved by the FAA. The individual also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. Passing a written test and a demonstration of flying ability are required. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.121-61.133 and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-15.title: Flight Engineer
00-15.description: To become certified as a Flight Engineer requires that the individual have either training or experience. Passing a written exam and a practical test and having a current medical certificate are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://umet-vets.dol.gov/flightengineer.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.31-63.43.

00-77.title: Flight Instructor
00-77.description: To obtain certification as a Flight Instructor, the individual must hold either a Commercial Pilot or Airline Transport Pilot certificate with appropriate aircraft and instrument ratings. Training is required as well as experience in the type of aircraft being rated. This license is valid for 2 years and may be renewed by one of several options, such as passing a practical test, documenting student success, or taking a refresher course. More details can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.181-61.199, www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ.

00-20.title: Flight Navigator
00-20.description: To become certified as a Flight Navigator, the individual must be at least 21 years old and have a medical certificate. He or she must have both training in flight navigation and practical experience. Passing written and practical tests are required as well as having a current medical certificate. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended, or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.51-63.61.

00-13.title: Ground Instructor
00-13.description: To obtain certification as a Ground Instructor, the individual must pass an aircraft navigation knowledge test and a test of the fundamentals of instructing, unless the person already is employed as a teacher or holds a teacher's certification. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.211-61.217.

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

00-06.title: Private Pilot
00-06.description: Obtaining a Private Pilot certificate (license) requires the individual to complete ground and flight training, have flight experience, obtain a medical certificate, and pass a written exam as well as a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. The FAA Advisory Circular, AC 61-12M, Student Pilot Guide, outlines general procedures for obtaining student and private pilot certificates. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.102-61.117, and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

44-BUR0000140.title: Burglar and Hold-up Alarm Agent
44-BUR0000140.description: Installs, repairs, maintains and updates burglar alarms and hold-up alarms in residences and businesses.
44-BUR0000140.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-FAI0000460.title: Fire Alarm Installer
44-FAI0000460.description: Installs, alters, repairs or renovates fire alarm systems.
44-FAI0000460.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

00-60.title: Medical Doctor
00-60.description: A ship's Medical Doctor is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A medical doctor must also hold a valid license as a physician or surgeon issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-60.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-OST0000870.title: Osteopathic Physician (D.O.)
44-OST0000870.description: Diagnoses and treats disease and disorders of the human body. Although osteopaths may specialize in a particular field of medicine, many choose to concentrate on impairments of the musculoskeleton system, focusing on afflictions of bones, muscles, ligaments or nerves.
44-OST0000870.agency: RI Department of Health · Board of Medical Licensure and Discipline

44-PHY0000930.title: Physician and Surgeon (Allopathic - M.D.)
44-PHY0000930.description: Diagnoses and treats disease and disorders of the human body. Examines patients and uses medical equipment, instruments and tests following standard medical procedures. Prescribes and administers medications as needed.
44-PHY0000930.agency: RI Department of Health · Board of Medical Licensure and Discipline

44-ARB0000040.title: Arborist
44-ARB0000040.description: Engages in tree surgery, tree pruning, tree removal, utility line clearance, and the care and maintenance of trees. Additional Pesticide Applicator license from DEM Division of Agriculture is required for use of pesticides.
44-ARB0000040.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Division of Forest Environment

44-ARC0000050.title: Architect
44-ARC0000050.description: Plans, designs and oversees construction of private residences, office buildings, theaters, factories and other structures. May specialize in a particular type of structure or project.
44-ARC0000050.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Design Professionals

00-48.title: Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-48.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must, while holding a license as a Third Assistant Engineer, complete one of the following: 360 days of service as an Assistant Engineer; or a minimum of 180 days as an Assistant Engineer and 360 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 360 days as Chief Engineer (Limited-Oceans). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-48.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-38.title: Second Mate - Upper Level
00-38.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Mate Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on ocean steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Third Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-38.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-BOX0000130.title: Boxer, Professional
44-BOX0000130.description: Participates in competitive boxing events, using the art of attack and defense using fists.
44-BOX0000130.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Commercial Licensing & Racing & Athletics

44-MMA0000725.title: Mixed Martial Arts Professional (MMA)
44-MMA0000725.description: Participates in competitive MMA events, using the art of attack and defense using fists and legs.
44-MMA0000725.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Commercial Licensing & Racing & Athletics

44-ATH0000070.title: Athletic Trainer
44-ATH0000070.description: Exercises, recommends diets, massages players' bodies, renders first aid, treats minor injuries of professional and amateur athletes to maintain maximum physical fitness for participation in athletic competition.
44-ATH0000070.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-65.title: Ship Radar Endorsement
00-65.description: The Ship Radar Endorsement is issued by the Federal Communications Commission to licensed commercial radio operators. This endorsement allows them to repair, maintain, or internally adjust ship radar equipment. Passing a written exam is required. For further information, see the FCC web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/sre.html.

44-BAR0000090.title: Barber
44-BAR0000090.description: Provides barber services for customers, including suggesting hair styles, cutting, trimming, shampooing, bleaching and dying hair and applying lotions and creams to customer's face and neck. Also includes giving shaves.
44-BAR0000090.agency: RI Department of Health · Office of Facilities Regulation

44-ELC0000370.title: Electrologist
44-ELC0000370.description: Removes hair from skin of patrons using an electric current applied to the body with a needle.
44-ELC0000370.agency: RI Department of Health · Office of Facilities Regulation

44-HAM0000535.title: Hairdresser, Cosmetologist, Esthetician, Manicurist
44-HAM0000535.description: Hairdressers and cosmetologists shampoo, cut and style hair, analyze the condition of the hair and advise patrons on hair care. Estheticians perform skin care services, skin analysis consultations, massage, makeup application. Manicurists clean, shape and polish fingernails and toenails.
44-HAM0000535.agency: RI Department of Health · Office of Facilities Regulation

44-BAR0000010.title: Bartenders
44-BAR0000010.description: A person who mixes and serves alcoholic drinks at a bar. All persons who sell or serve alcoholic beverages; anyone serving in a supervisory capacity over those who sell or serve alcoholic beverages; anyone whose job description entails the checking of identification for the purchase of alcoholic beverages; and valet parking staff shall be required to complete certified alcohol serving training within sixty (60) days of the commencement of his or her employment and must attain a minimum score of seventy-five percent (75%) and are to be recertified every three years.
44-BAR0000010.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Liquor Enforcement and Compliance

44-CLT0000220.title: Clinical Laboratory Technician
44-CLT0000220.description: Performs routine tests in medical laboratory to provide data for use in diagnosis and treatment of disease, including qualitative and quantitative analysis of body fluids, such as blood, urine and spinal fluid.
44-CLT0000220.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-21.title: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T1
00-21.description: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T1) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. Further information can be found at the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-24.title: General Radiotelephone Operator License - PG
00-24.description: General Radiotelephone Operator License (PG) is issued for a lifetime and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-26.title: GMDSS Radio Maintainer's License - DM
00-26.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Maintainer's License (DM) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-27.title: GMDSS Radio Operator's License - DO
00-27.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Operator's License (DO) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-25.title: Marine Radio Operator Permit - MP
00-25.description: Marine Radio Operator Permit (MP) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-58.title: Radio Officer
00-58.description: The Radio Officer's license is issued to applicants who have a valid Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license as first or second class radiotelegraph operator (T1, T2). Certain officers are required to hold Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) certification issued by the FCC. Further information can be found at theUSCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-58.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-75.title: Restricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit (RP)
00-75.description: RP holders are authorized to operate most aircraft and aeronautical ground stations. They can also operate marine radiotelephone stations aboard pleasure craft (other than those carrying more than six passengers for hire on the Great Lakes or bays or tidewaters or in the open sea) when operator licensing is required. To obtain this permit, you must be able to speak and hear; and keep a written log; and be familiar with provisions of applicable treaties, laws and rules which govern the radio station you will operate. For further information, see the Federal Communications web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/rp.html.

00-22.title: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T2
00-22.description: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T2) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-23.title: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T3
00-23.description: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T3) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-57.title: Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-57.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,080 days at sea with 720 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-57.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-56.title: Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-56.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,440 days at sea with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer and 950 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm.
00-56.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-19.title: Inspector's Authorization
00-19.description: To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an Aircraft Mechanic A & P certificate for at least 3 years. For further information, see web site http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, parts 65.91-65.95.

00-41.title: Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels - OUPV
00-41.description: To become licensed as an Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels requires specific experience -- Near Coastal or Inland as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. For complete details see the USCG web page http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at website http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50846230377+3+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve or http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-41.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-42.title: Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels - OUTV
00-42.description: To become licensed as a an Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) or 2nd Class Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) requires specific experience - Oceans (Domestic Route), Near Coastal or Inland, as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Details can be found on the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-42.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-cdl.title: Commercial Drivers License (CDL)
44-cdl.description: Commercial Drivers Licenses are issued by state departments but are similar from state to state, since the minimum requirements of the licenses and endorsements are set centrally. For more information contact the state DMV or https://cms.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/commercial-drivers-license/how-do-i-get-commercial-drivers-license.
44-cdl.agency: Rhode Island Department of Revenue · Division of Motor Vehicles

44-LIN0000650.title: Line Cleaner
44-LIN0000650.description: Cleans and sterilizes machinery, utensils and equipment used to process and serve malt beverages. Drains machines or tanks, rinses with water, scrubs with cleaning tools or preparations and rinses.
44-LIN0000650.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Liquor Enforcement and Compliance

44-FAD0000440.title: Family Day Care Home Provider
44-FAD0000440.description: Provides care of four to six children for any part of a 24-hour day (or seven or eight children with an assistant) in a family day care home. (See Family Group Day Care Home Provider license for care of nine to twelve children).
44-FAD0000440.agency: RI Department of Human Services · Office of Child Care Licensing Team

44-FAG0000450.title: Family Group Day Care Home Provider
44-FAG0000450.description: Provides care for nine to twelve children for any part of a 24-hour day in a family day care home. (See Family Day Child Care Provider license for care of less than nine children).
44-FAG0000450.agency: RI Department of Human Services · Office of Child Care Licensing Team

44-CHI0000180.title: Chiropractic Physician
44-CHI0000180.description: Employs a system of palpating and adjusting the articulations of the human spinal column and its appendages by hand and electro-mechanical appliances, and the employment of corrective orthopedics and dietetics for the elimination of the cause of disease.
44-CHI0000180.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-CLA0000190.title: Claim Adjuster (Insurance)
44-CLA0000190.description: Investigates claims against insurance companies for personal, casualty, property loss or damage and attempts to negotiate out-of-court settlement. Examines claim forms, hospital and police records, and interviews the claimant and/or witnesses. Three lines of authority: commercial, property, and workers' compensation.
44-CLA0000190.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Insurance Division

44-CLH0000200.title: Clinical Histologic Technician
44-CLH0000200.description: Prepare specimens of human and animal tissues for microscopic examinations. May perform other routine operations in the pathology laboratory, such as preserving specimens.
44-CLH0000200.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-ATC0001440.title: Athletic Coach
44-ATC0001440.description: Valid for service as a coach to school district athletic teams.
44-ATC0001440.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-DEA0000250.title: Dealer (Finfish, Lobster, Shellfish, Multipurpose)
44-DEA0000250.description: Purchases fish from commercial fishers for resale to retail outlets.
44-DEA0000250.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Boat Registration and Licensing

44-FIS0000490.title: Fisher, Commercial
44-FIS0000490.description: Seeds, cultivates, transplants, stocks, catches or gathers aquatic life of any kind for sale.
44-FIS0000490.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Boat Registration and Licensing

44-LIV0000670.title: Live Bait Seller
44-LIV0000670.description: Sells minnows to individuals for use as fishing bait.
44-LIV0000670.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Boat Registration and Licensing

44-NCS0000010.title: Nuisance Control Specialist
44-NCS0000010.description: Licensed to remove and exclude wildlife from homes and businesses.
44-NCS0000010.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Division of Fish and Wildlife

44-TPP0001290.title: Trapper, Commercial
44-TPP0001290.description: Traps animals for pelts, live sale, bounty or to relocate them in other areas. Sets traps with bait, scent or camouflage and in patterns according to size, species, habits and environs of animal sought or according to reasons for trapping.
44-TPP0001290.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Boat Registration and Licensing

44-ASB0000060.title: Asbestos Abatement Contractor/Supervisor/Worker
44-ASB0000060.description: Removes, encapsulates or encloses asbestos and asbestos containing material found in ceilings, walls, beams, boilers and other structures. Follows hazardous waste handling guidelines.
44-ASB0000060.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-LSR0001370.title: Lead-Safe Remodeler/Renovator
44-LSR0001370.description: Responsible for performing lead hazard control activities in accordance with the Rhode Island Rules and Regulations for Lead Poisoning Prevention [R23-24.6-PB] and the EPA Renovate, Repair and Painting Final Rule that was effective as of April 22, 2010 for which Rhode Island has delegation. A lead safe remodeler/renovator is also responsible for direct on-site supervision of lead hazard control work in regulated facilities.
44-LSR0001370.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-HOI0000550.title: Hoisting Engineer
44-HOI0000550.description: Uses one or more of the following: conveyer belt, concrete belt, payload backhoe, overhead electric crane or drilling rig in order to move workers and materials for construction, sawmill and mining operations.
44-HOI0000550.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-SNT0001140.title: School Nurse-Teacher
44-SNT0001140.description: Plans school health program with medical and school authorities. Participates in medical examinations and reviews findings. Instructs classes in health. Works with school personnel in meeting social, emotional and physical needs of school children.
44-SNT0001140.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-TES0001261.title: Teacher (Secondary)
44-TES0001261.description: Plans and presents programs of instruction using materials and methods appropriate to age and learning style. Elementary teachers work with children from kindergarten through eighth grade in many subject areas. Secondary school teachers instruct students in one or more areas of specialization. Certificates are issued to qualified applicants in certain specialties, including reading, music, art, and secondary school subjects.
44-TES0001261.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-TEC0001390.title: Teacher: General Subject Matter Substituteá
44-TEC0001390.description: Valid for service as a 'day-to-day' substitute teacher.
44-TEC0001390.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-TEC0001400.title: Teacher: Special Subjects (PK-12)
44-TEC0001400.description: Provide instruction in the following subject areas: art, music, theater, dance, physical education, health, library/media, home economics, technology education.
44-TEC0001400.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-DEH0000260.title: Dental Hygienist
44-DEH0000260.description: Works under direct supervision of a dentist to provide direct patient care. Removes deposits and stains from patients' teeth, exposes and develops dental X-ray film, performs various other preventative and therapeutic services. Instructs individuals and groups in proper oral hygiene.
44-DEH0000260.agency: RI Department of Health · Board of Denistry

44-DEN0000270.title: Dentist
44-DEN0000270.description: Treats diseases or abnormalities of teeth and tissues of the mouth. May be a general practitioner or limit his/her practice to a specialty (i.e.., endodontics, pediadontics, orthodontics).
44-DEN0000270.agency: RI Department of Health · Board of Denistry

44-DIE0000280.title: Dietitian/Nutritionist
44-DIE0000280.description: Organizes, plans and conducts food service or nutritional programs to assist in promotion of health and control of disease.
44-DIE0000280.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-ELC0000350.title: Electrical Sign Installer
44-ELC0000350.description: Installs, alters, repairs or renovates electrical signs. Consults with clients and follows electrical plans for proper installation.
44-ELC0000350.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-ELE0000360.title: Electrician
44-ELE0000360.description: Installs, alters, repairs or renovates electrical systems. Consults with clients and follows electrical plans for proper installation.
44-ELE0000360.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-ELM0000390.title: Elevator Mechanic
44-ELM0000390.description: Assembles, installs, repairs, and maintains, electric and hydraulic freight and passenger elevators, escalators, and dumbwaiters.
44-ELM0000390.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Division of Occupational Safety - Elevator Unit

44-FUN0000510.title: Funeral Director/Embalmer
44-FUN0000510.description: Prepares dead human remains for burial or disposal. Maintains the funeral establishment and sells funeral service merchandise to the public. May counsel and comfort relatives and friends, prepare casket and transport the deceased for services and burial. Prior to 1996 there were separate licenses for funeral directors and for embalmers.
44-FUN0000510.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-EMT0000400.title: Emergency Medical Technician
44-EMT0000400.description: An emergency medical technician administers stabilization, transportation and medical care to sick or injured persons. All EMTs provide basic life support. The EMT-C is the primary provider of advanced life support in Rhode Island. The Paramedic has greater knowledge of life support and latitude to institute advanced life support.
44-EMT0000400.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-ENT0000430.title: Environmental Lead Inspector-Technician
44-ENT0000430.description: Responsible for conducting on-site activities associated with environmental lead inspections in accordance with the Rhode Island Rules and Regulations for Lead Poisoning Prevention [R23-24.6-PB]. Some inspections performed by an Inspector Technician/Technician-in Training must be reviewed and approved by an Environmental Lead Inspector before the report is issued. An Inspector Technician/Technician-in Training may not independently issue a report or make recommendations.
44-ENT0000430.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-ENI0000420.title: Environmental Lead Professionals
44-ENI0000420.description: Responsible for overall planning and implementation of environmental lead inspections in accordance with the Rhode Island Rules and Regulations for Lead Poisoning Prevention [R23-24.6-PB]. Inspectors may also employ certified Environmental Lead Inspector Technicians and Technicians-in-Training to assist with these activities.
44-ENI0000420.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-RMS0000100.title: Radon Mitigation Specialist
44-RMS0000100.description: Evaluates diagnostic tests to determine appropriate radon or radon progeny mitigation strategies, designs and supervises the installation of mitigation systems.
44-RMS0000100.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-RMW0000100.title: Radon Mitigation Worker
44-RMW0000100.description: Helps install radon or radon progeny mitigation systems. Radon mitigation worker services must be performed under the on-site supervision of a licensed Radon Mitigation Specialist.
44-RMW0000100.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-RMW000100.title: Radon Mitigation Worker
44-RMW000100.description: Helps install radon or radon progeny mitigation systems. Radon mitigation worker services must be performed under the on-site supervision of a licensed Radon Mitigation Specialist.
44-RMW000100.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-SAN0001100.title: Sanitarian
44-SAN0001100.description: Plans, organizes, manages, executes and evaluates one or more of the many diverse elements comprising the field of environmental health. A sanitarian may construct and utilize environmental health programs and set health and sanitation standards for public facilities. DEREGULATED AS OF JUNE 20, 2015
44-SAN0001100.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-NSD0000160.title: Nursery Stock Dealer
44-NSD0000160.description: Offers woody plants (trees and shrubs) for retail or wholesale trade.
44-NSD0000160.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Division of Agriculture

44-NUR0000800.title: Nurseryworker
44-NUR0000800.description: Cultivates woody plants (trees and shrubs) for retail or wholesale trade.
44-NUR0000800.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Division of Agriculture

44-INV0000570.title: Investment Adviser Representative (IAR)
44-INV0000570.description: Any person who, for compensation, engages in the business of advising others, either directly or through publications or writings, as to the value of securities or as to the advisability of investing in, purchasing, or selling securities, manages accounts or portfolios of clients, solicits, offers, or negotiates for the sale of or sells investment advisory services, or who, for compensation and as part of a regular business, issues or promulgates analyses or reports concerning securities.
44-INV0000570.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Securities

00-FinOpL.title: Series 39 - Direct Participation Programs Limited Principal
00-FinOpL.description: Covered supervisory activities and products include regulatory compliance over sales of: ?Direct participation program limited partnerships (e.g., real estate, oil and gas, and equipment leasing) ?Limited liability companies ?S corporations In addition to sales supervision, the Series 39 qualifies a principal for the overall supervision of a firm’s investment banking and securities business—including compliance, underwriting and advertising—for those activities specially covered by each supervisory principal’s license.

44-WIP0001340.title: Wildlife Propagator
44-WIP0001340.description: Raises game species for wildlife re-stocking, sport, retail market and laboratories.
44-WIP0001340.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Boat Registration and Licensing

44-WIR0001350.title: Wildlife Rehabilitator
44-WIR0001350.description: Nurses and cares for sick and injured wildlife.
44-WIR0001350.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Division of Fish and Wildlife

44-FSM0000010.title: Food Safety Manager
44-FSM0000010.description: Responsible for operating a food establishment in compliance with all relevant federal and state rules and regulations pertaining to food, and assure that all employees engaged in food preparation do so in a manner consistent with food safety.
44-FSM0000010.agency: RI Department of Health · Center for Food Protection

44-FRC0000010.title: Fundraising Counsel
44-FRC0000010.description: Any person who for compensation consults with a charitable organization or who plans, manages, advises, or assists with respect to the solicitation of contributions for or on behalf of a charitable organization, but who does not have access to contributions or other receipts from a solicitation and who does not solicit. Bona fide volunteers or employees of a charitable organization, or an attorney-at-law retained by a charitable organization, shall not be deemed a fund raising counsel.
44-FRC0000010.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Securities

44-PFR0000010.title: Professional Fund Raiser
44-PFR0000010.description: Any person who directly or indirectly for compensation or other consideration plans, manages, conducts, carries on, or assists in connection with a solicitation for charitable purposes or individually solicits or who employs or otherwise engages on any basis another person to solicit for or on behalf of any charitable organization, or who engages in the business of, or holds himself, herself or itself out to persons as independently engaged in the business of soliciting for the charitable purpose. Bona fide volunteers or employees of a charitable organization or fund raising counsel shall not be deemed a professional fund raiser.
44-PFR0000010.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Securities

44-PSC0000010.title: Professional Solicitor
44-PSC0000010.description: Any person who is employed or retained for compensation by a professional fund raiser to solicit contributions for charitable purposes. Bona fide employees of a charitable organization or fund raising counsel shall not be deemed a professional solicitor.
44-PSC0000010.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Securities

44-GCL0000010.title: Genetic Counselor
44-GCL0000010.description: Practice of genetic counseling means a communication process, conducted by one or more appropriately trained individuals that may include: (i) Obtaining and evaluating individual, family, and medical histories to determine genetic risk for genetic/medical conditions and diseases in a patient, the patient’s offspring, and other family members; (ii) Discussing the features, natural history, means of diagnosis, genetic and environmental factors, and management of risk for genetic/medical conditions and diseases; (iii) Identifying, ordering, and coordinating genetic laboratory tests as appropriate for the genetic assessment; (iv) Integrating genetic laboratory test results and other diagnostic studies with personal and family medical history to assess and communicate risk factors for genetic/medical conditions and diseases; (v) Explaining the clinical implications of genetic laboratory tests and other diagnostic studies and their results; (vi) Evaluating the client’s or family’s responses to the condition or risk of recurrence and providing client-centered counseling and anticipatory guidance; (vii) Identifying and utilizing community resources that provide medical, educational, financial, and psychosocial support and advocacy; (viii) Providing written documentation of medical, genetic, and counseling information for families and healthcare professionals; and (ix) When necessary,…

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

44-GCL0000010.agency: RI Department of Health · Genetic Counselors Licensing

44-LHC0000610.title: Lead Hazard Professionals
44-LHC0000610.description: Responsible for overall planning and implementation of lead hazard reduction activities in accordance with the Rhode Island Rules and Regulations for Lead Poisoning Prevention [R23-24.6-PB]. Contractors may also employ licensed Lead Hazard Reduction Site Supervisors, Workers and Workers-in-Training to assist with these activities.
44-LHC0000610.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-LHS0000620.title: Lead Hazard Reduction Site Supervisor
44-LHS0000620.description: Responsible for on-site oversight of lead hazard reduction activities in accordance with the Rhode Island Rules and Regulations for Lead Poisoning Prevention [R23-24.6-PB]. A site supervisor is employed by and works under the general direction of a Lead Hazard Reduction Contractor. A site supervisor is also responsible for supervision of licensed Lead Hazard Reduction Workers and Workers-in-Training when the Contractor is not present.
44-LHS0000620.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-LHW0000630.title: Lead Hazard Reduction Worker
44-LHW0000630.description: Responsible for performing lead hazard reduction activities in accordance with the Rhode Island Rules and Regulations for Lead Positioning Prevention [R23-24.6-PB]. Workers and Workers-in-Training must be employed by a licensed Lead Hazard Reduction Contractor and work under the supervision of the Contractor or a licensed Lead Hazard Reduction Site Supervisor.
44-LHW0000630.agency: RI Department of Health · Division of Food, Water & Environment

44-LCN0000010.title: Lactation Consultant
44-LCN0000010.description: Health care professional who specializes in the clinical management of breastfeeding for childbearing families.
44-LCN0000010.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-NMI0000790.title: Nurse-Midwife
44-NMI0000790.description: Provides care for expectant mothers with apparently normal pregnancies. Furnishes professional medical care during the pregnancy, labor, delivery and after-birth phases for both the mother and the newborn infant.
44-NMI0000790.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-ALR0000010.title: Assisted Living Residence Administrator
44-ALR0000010.description: Responsible for the day to day adminstration or operation of an assisted living residence.
44-ALR0000010.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-CNA0000810.title: Nursing Assistant (Aide)
44-CNA0000810.description: Gives personal care and related health care and assistance to patients under the direction of nursing and medical staff.
44-CNA0000810.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-NHA0000820.title: Nursing Home Administrator
44-NHA0000820.description: Directs the medical, nursing and administrative activities of a nursing home to ensure that patients receive quality care and staff have the facilities, equipment and support necessary to meet that goal. An administrator is responsible for developing policies and procedures for nursing home activities, establishing and following budgeting guidelines and personnel management.
44-NHA0000820.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-swn691.title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
44-swn691.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-swn681.title: Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker
44-swn681.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-HEA0000540.title: Hearing Aid Dealer and Fitter
44-HEA0000540.description: Examines, evaluates, and confers with customers about individual hearing needs and sells customers the appropriate hearing aid. May also be responsible for demonstrating, repairing and replacing hearing aids.
44-HEA0000540.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-OIL0000840.title: Oil Burnerperson
44-OIL0000840.description: Installs and services automatic oil burners in furnaces in homes and commercial establishments, using hand tools and pipe threading tools. Connects pipe to the oil storage tank, installs thermostatic controls, adjusts flame and determines causes of faulty operation.
44-OIL0000840.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-RFG0001080.title: Refrigeration Mechanic
44-RFG0001080.description: Lays out, fabricates, installs and maintains piping in refrigeration systems. Air conditioning mechanics do similar work but in air conditioning systems.
44-RFG0001080.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

00-Ins.title: NIPR Insurance Registry
00-Ins.description: Licensed Insurance Occupations must also be registered at the federal level.

44-INS0000560.title: Insurance Producer
44-INS0000560.description: Sells insurance of a variety of types and from different companies to new and present clients, recommending amount and type of coverage based on analysis of prospect's circumstances. May collect premiums and keep record of payments. This license is required for any individual who sells insurance in Rhode Island, even though their base of operations is not in the state.
44-INS0000560.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Insurance Division

44-SUR0001230.title: Surplus Line Broker
44-SUR0001230.description: A licensed insurance agent who is also licensed as a surplus line broker may procure policies of insurance, except life and health and accident, from insurers which are not authorized to transact business in the state.
44-SUR0001230.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Insurance Division

44-INT0000100.title: Interpreter for the Deaf
44-INT0000100.description: Interprets English into American Sign Language (ASL) or interprets American Sign Language into English, or interprets English to or from a visual gesture system.
44-INT0000100.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-TES0001260.title: Teacher (Elementary)
44-TES0001260.description: Plans and presents programs of instruction using materials and methods appropriate to age and learning style. Elementary teachers work with children from kindergarten through eighth grade in many subject areas. Secondary school teachers instruct students in one or more areas of specialization. Certificates are issued to qualified applicants in certain specialties, including reading, music, art, and secondary school subjects.
44-TES0001260.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-LAR0000600.title: Landscape Architect
44-LAR0000600.description: Plans and designs the development of land areas such as residential and recreational areas, parks and public facilities. Strives to develop land areas that are attractive, functional and environmentally appropriate, analyzes the natural elements such as climate, drainage, soil and vegetation, and protects the public health, safety and welfare.
44-LAR0000600.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects

44-ATT0000080.title: Attorney and Counselor
44-ATT0000080.description: Advises individuals or business enterprises on legal problems, draws up legal documents, examines legal data to determine advisability of defending or prosecuting lawsuits. May represent client in court or before quasi-judicial or administrative agencies.
44-ATT0000080.agency: RI Supreme Court · Board of Bar Examiners

44-LIF0000640.title: Lifeguard
44-LIF0000640.description: Monitors activities in swimming areas to prevent accidents and provide assistance to swimmers. Cautions swimmers regarding unsafe areas, rescues swimmers in danger of drowning and administers first aid.
44-LIF0000640.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Division of Parks and Recreation

44-BEE0000100.title: Beekeeper
44-BEE0000100.description: Raises bees to produce honey and pollinate crops. Assembles beehives, stocks with bees, destroys diseased bee colonies, extracts and sells honey. A Honeybee Hive Entry Permit (fee $50.00) is required to bring bees in from another state.
44-BEE0000100.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Division of Agriculture

44-LPN0000770.title: Nurse, Licensed Practical
44-LPN0000770.description: Cares for ill, injured, convalescent and/or disabled patients under the direction of physicians and registered nurses. LPN's are often responsible for taking and recording a patient's temperature, blood pressure and pulse.
44-LPN0000770.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-MAR0000710.title: Marriage and Family Therapist
44-MAR0000710.description: Treats and rehabilitates individuals and families with problems in communication, relationship skills and behavior within the family.
44-MAR0000710.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-MAS0000720.title: Massage Therapist
44-MAS0000720.description: Massages customers and administers other body conditioning treatments for hygienic or remedial purposes. May administer heat, ultraviolet or infrared or water treatments on request of customer or instructions of physician.
44-MAS0000720.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-52.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations
00-47.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-49.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-NUC0000740.title: Nuclear Medicine Technologist
44-NUC0000740.description: Administers a radioactive substance to a human being for diagnostic purposes and performs associated procedures.
44-NUC0000740.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-10.title: Nuclear Facility Operator
00-10.description: Nuclear Facility Operators are required to have either training or experience to become licensed. They must pass a medical exam, a written test, and an operating test. Although the license is granted for 6 years, licensees must pass another medical exam every two years and an operating test annually. Also, they must undergo requalification training while employed. Nuclear Facility Senior Operators have additional experience and pass another exam to be promoted from Nuclear Facility Operators. Further information can be found at the web site: http://www.nrc.gov/reactors/operator-licensing.html

44-NUA0000750.title: Nurse Anesthetist
44-NUA0000750.description: Administers pre-operative and post-operative anesthesia, monitors patients during anesthesia, administers specific drugs, manages fluids in intravenous therapy and manages respiratory care under the supervision of a physician.
44-NUA0000750.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-NUP0000760.title: Nurse Practitioner
44-NUP0000760.description: Provides basic primary health care utilizing independent knowledge of physical assessment and management of health care and illnesses. The practice includes prescriptive privileges and includes collaboration with other licensed health care professionals, such as physicians, pharmacists, dentists, and nurses.
44-NUP0000760.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-63.title: Hospital Corpsman
00-63.description: A Hospital Corpsman is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A hospital corpsman must have U.S. military experience as and a rating of hospital corpsman or Health Services Technician or equivalent. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-63.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-OCC0000830.title: Occupational Therapist
44-OCC0000830.description: Plans, organizes and provides a program of services to individuals whose lives have been impaired by physical, psychological or developmental problems. The therapist usually works as part of a medical team to analyze patients' needs and to select appropriate activities to help patients develop independence, return to work, restore basic functions and adjust to disabilities.
44-OCC0000830.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-OPC0000850.title: Optician
44-OPC0000850.description: Reads eyeglass lens and frame specifications from prescription, selects lens blanks, sets up and operates machines to fabricate lenses to specifications. Mounts lenses in frames, inspects for conformity to specifications.
44-OPC0000850.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-OPM0000860.title: Optometrist
44-OPM0000860.description: Examines, diagnoses and treats conditions of the visual system. Prescribes corrective procedures to improve and correct vision utilizing vision therapy and training, corrective lenses and control of the visual environment.
44-OPM0000860.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-PRO0000990.title: Prosthetist
44-PRO0000990.description: Provides care to patients with partial or total absence of limb with devices known as prostheses. DEREGULATED AS OF JUNE 30, 2015
44-PRO0000990.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-OTA0000010.title: Occupational Therapy Assistant
44-OTA0000010.description: Plans, organizes and provides a program of services to individuals whose lives have been impaired by physical, psychological or developmental problems. The therapist usually works as part of a medical team to analyze patients' needs and to select appropriate activities to help patients develop independence, return to work, restore basic functions and adjust to disabilities.
44-OTA0000010.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-PHA0000890.title: Pharmacist
44-PHA0000890.description: Interprets prescriptions, compounds medications and dispenses to customers medications ordered by physicians, dentists or other authorized prescriber. May be asked to advise patients and prescribers on the therapeutic values, contents and uses of drugs and related devices.
44-PHA0000890.agency: RI Department of Health · RI Board of Pharmacy

44-PHT0000895.title: Pharmacy Technician I & II
44-PHT0000895.description: Supports pharmacist by providing nonjudgmental technical services concerned with the preparation of drugs under the direct supervision and responsibility of a pharmacist.
44-PHT0000895.agency: RI Department of Health · RI Board of Pharmacy

44-PTH0000900.title: Physical Therapist
44-PTH0000900.description: After physician referral, plans, monitors and administers physical therapy for patients to restore bodily functions, relieve pain and prevent disability due to disease, injury or other disabilities.
44-PTH0000900.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-80.title: Marine Physician Assistant
00-80.description: A Marine Physician Assistant is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A physician assistant must also have training as a physician's assistant or nurse practitioner. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-80.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-PHA0000920.title: Physician Assistant
44-PHA0000920.description: Physician assistant provides a broad range of services under the supervision of a licensed physician including management of illnesses, preventive and emergency services and personal and family counseling.
44-PHA0000920.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-31.title: Tankerman
00-31.description: Tankerman refers to several endorsements or qualified ratings to Merchant Marine Documents (MMD). All Tankerman endorsements require qualifying experience, training in firefighting and cargo (dangerous liquids or liquefied gasses), and passing an exam. Endorsements include Tankerman - Person-In-Charge (Tankerman PIC), Tankerman-Engineer, Tankerman Assistant, and Tankerman - PIC (Barge). Tankerman endorsements are valid for the duration of the MMD, which is issued for 5 years. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR13.109) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02.html.
00-31.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-FPS0000475.title: Fire Protection Sprinkler Fitter
44-FPS0000475.description: Lays out, fabricates, installs and maintains piping for fire protection systems.
44-FPS0000475.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-IRR0000970.title: Irrigator
44-IRR0000970.description: Sells, designs, consults, installs, maintains, alters, repair, or engages in business of irrigation (an assembly of component parts permanently installed with and for the distribution and conservation of water for the purpose of irrigating any type of landscape vegetation in any location or for the purpose of dust reduction or erosion control. This includes parts used in the application and installation of drip systems. Irrigation work means the connection to the backflow prevention devices.) upon any properties public or private either by contract or agreement with the owner, lessee, tenant or agent of those premises.
44-IRR0000970.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-PIP0000950.title: Pipefitter
44-PIP0000950.description: Lays out, fabricates, installs and maintains piping in steam, hot water and heating systems. Fire protection sprinkler fitter does similar work but in fire protection systems.
44-PIP0000950.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-PLU0000960.title: Plumber
44-PLU0000960.description: Installs, alters and repairs pipes, fittings and fixtures for heating water, water supply and waste disposals in homes and commercial buildings. Follows building plans and instructions, lays out job and works with tools.
44-PLU0000960.agency: RI Department of Labor and Training · Professional Regulation

44-POD0000970.title: Podiatrist
44-POD0000970.description: Diagnoses and treats foot diseases and disorders by performing basic medical and surgical procedures. Examines the foot and lower leg and diagnoses ailments.
44-POD0000970.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-CON0000010.title: Constable
44-CON0000010.description: Serve or executes writs and process in such capacity for any court of the state, anywhere in the state, subject to any terms and limitations as set forth by the court, and in such number as determined by the chief judge of the district court.
44-CON0000010.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Commercial Licensing & Racing & Athletics

00-05.title: Customs Broker
00-05.description: Customs brokers must pass an exam to obtain a license. Further information can be found at the US Customs Service web site: http://www.customs.gov/xp/cgov/import/broker_management/.

00-59.title: Purser
00-59.description: The Purser, one of a ship's staff officers, is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A Junior Assistant Purser requires no experience. A Senior Assistant Purser requires 180 days, a Purser requires 360 days, and a Chief Purser requires 720 days of service aboard vessels while performing duties related to the purser's office. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-59.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-REB0001060.title: Real Estate Broker
44-REB0001060.description: Manages or works for real estate offices that lists, purchases, sells, rent, leases real estate for clients. Negotiates sales, manages rental properties, offers broker price opinions (BPO) and provides purchasing information.
44-REB0001060.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Commercial Licensing & Racing & Athletics

44-PSY0001000.title: Psychologist, Private Practice
44-PSY0001000.description: Studies individual and group behaviors or mental processes in order to gain an understanding and explanation of behavior to assist in positive change. Often interviews and evaluates individuals, conducts research and experiments and counsels clients.
44-PSY0001000.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-SPY0001150.title: School Psychologist
44-SPY0001150.description: Evaluates needs of average, gifted, and disturbed children and children with disabilities within educational system and plans and carries out programs to enable children to attain maximum achievement and adjustment. Conducts diagnostic studies, consults with parents and school personnel, plans special placement or other treatment programs.
44-SPY0001150.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-PTA0000910.title: Physical Therapist Assistant
44-PTA0000910.description: Administers physical therapy treatments to patients, working under direction of and as assistant to physical therapist.
44-PTA0000910.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-RAD0001030.title: Radiation Therapist
44-RAD0001030.description: Uses the direct application of ionizing radiation to human beings for therapeutic purposes.
44-RAD0001030.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-RAG0001040.title: Radiographer
44-RAG0001040.description: Produces x-ray images of parts of the human body to assist physicians in diagnosing medical problems. Prepare and position patients, use protective devices, control x-ray machine, and develop film.
44-RAG0001040.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-RES0001070.title: Real Estate Salesperson
44-RES0001070.description: Sells, leases, and rents property for clients on a commission or fee basis. To sell property, often accompanies clients to property sites, quotes purchase price and compiles real estate contracts, and leases.
44-RES0001070.agency: RI Department of Business Regulation · Division of Commercial Licensing & Racing & Athletics

44-MTH0000010.title: Music Therapist
44-MTH0000010.description: Practices the clinical and evidence based use of music interventions to accomplish individualized goals within a therapeutic relationship through an individualized music therapy treatment plan for the client that identifies the goals, objectives, and potential strategies of the music therapy services appropriate for the client using music therapy interventions, which may include music improvisation, receptive music listening, song writing, lyric discussion, music and imagery, music performance, learning through music, and movement to music.
44-MTH0000010.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-RES0001090.title: Respiratory Care Practitioner
44-RES0001090.description: Implements treatment of patients with disabilities, disorders or injuries of cardiopulmonary system or during convalescence to relieve pain, restore functions, prevent muscular deconditioning and maintain maximum performance.
44-RES0001090.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-61.title: Professional Nurse
00-61.description: A ship's Professional Nurse is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A professional nurse must also hold a valid license as a registered nurse issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-61.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-RNU0000780.title: Nurse, Registered
44-RNU0000780.description: Observes, assesses and records symptoms, reactions and progress of ill, injured or convalescent patients. Administers medications, assists in convalescence and rehabilitation, instructs patients and their families, and helps individuals and groups to improve or maintain their health. Nursing actions including teaching and counseling are directed toward the promotion, maintenance and restoration of health and evaluation of the patient's response to nursing actions and medical regimen of care.
44-RNU0000780.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

44-PSY0002000.title: Psychiatric and Mental Health Clinical Nurse Specialist
44-PSY0002000.description: Uses independent knowledge and management of mental health and illnesses. The practice may include prescription privileges within the scope of their practice. The practice may include collaboration with other licensed health care professionals, including but not limited to psychiatrists, psychologists, physicians, pharmacists, and nurses.
44-PSY0002000.agency: RI Department of Health · Health Professions Regulation

00-03.title: Able Seaman - AB
00-03.description: Requirements for an Able Seaman license include a medical certificate of excellent health, and a certificate attesting to vision, color perception, and general physical condition. While no experience or formal schooling is required, training at a union-operated school is the best source. With experience at sea, and perhaps union-sponsored training, an ordinary seaman with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) can pass the Able Seaman exam and move up with 3 years of service. Please see the U.S. Coast Guard web site at: http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, the Veteran's Employment and Training Service (VETS) web site at http://umet-vets.dol.gov/ableseaman.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html
00-03.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-30.title: Lifeboatman - LBMAN
00-30.description: A person with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) with one year of experience at sea in the deck department, two years experience in any other department on vessels greater than 100 gross tons, or who has completed a USCG approved course and 3 months of sea experience may take written and practical exams to be endorsed with the qualified rating of Lifeboatman (LB). An MMD with a qualified rating is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through documented recent experience, pass an exam, or complete a training course. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR12.10-7) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-30.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-33.title: Merchant Mariner's Document - MMD
00-33.description: The United States Coast Guard issues a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) to unlicensed personnel who support the operation of a vessel. Unqualified ratings are issued to entry level individuals who typically have little or no sea service for the following rating types: ordinary seaman (deck department), wiper (engineering department), or food handler (steward's department). Qualified ratings are issued based on previous sea service in a particular department or specialized training. Qualified ratings for members in the deck department are issued by rating type (e.g. Able Seaman) and vessel type restrictions (e.g. sail vessels or offshore supply vessels). Qualified ratings for members in the engineering department are issued by type (e.g. Qualified Member of the Engine Department) and specific rating (e.g. oiler, fireman/watertender, junior engineer, deck engine mechanic, or engineman). Other ratings are issued for specialized training or experience, such as Lifeboatman, Tankerman, or GMDSS At-Sea Maintainer. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-33.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-04.title: Ordinary Seaman
00-04.description: An Ordinary Seaman is a person holding a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) issued by the United States Coast Guard without qualified ratings. This is an entry level MMD and does not require maritime experience or a physical examination, but will require proof that the applicant has passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs. While no training is required, a union-operated school can provide useful background knowledge. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-04.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-32.title: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED
00-32.description: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED A person with a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) having at least 6 months of underway service working as a wiper or coal passer in the engineering department may take a written exam and at least one rating exam (Fireman/Watertender, Oiler, Deck Engineer, Junior Engineer, Refrigeration Engineer, Electrician, Machinist, or Pumpman) to be endorsed as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Additional experience is required for some endorsements. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.15-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-32.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

44-CAT0000150.title: Livestock Dealer
44-CAT0000150.description: Buys, sells, and/or transports bovine animals to be sold or used for food.
44-CAT0000150.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management · Division of Agriculture

44-ADM0000030.title: Administrator, Special Education
44-ADM0000030.description: Formulates special education programs and policies for schools, public agencies and state institutions, relating to education and training of students with mental or physical disabilities. Reviews existing programs, revises and formulates policies such as screening, placement and education of students.
44-ADM0000030.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-ADM0001370.title: Director of Curriculum and Instruction
44-ADM0001370.description: Valid for service as an administrator of school district curriculum and instructional programs.For information on qulaifications, fees and applications, visit
44-ADM0001370.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-PRI0000980.title: Principal, School
44-PRI0000980.description: Directs and coordinates educational, administrative, counseling and extracurricular activities of elementary or secondary school, evaluates educational programs and maintains parent/community relations.
44-PRI0000980.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-RSC0001410.title: Reading Specialist/Consultant (PK-12)á
44-RSC0001410.description: Diagnosis and remediate disabilities at the elementary and/or secondary level; teach developmental reading at the secondary level; implement reading programs K-12 as classroom consultant.
44-RSC0001410.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-ADM0001420.title: Reading Supervisor/Director
44-ADM0001420.description: Valid for service as a reading supervisor or coordinator of reading programs.
44-ADM0001420.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-ADM0001430.title: School Business Administrator
44-ADM0001430.description: Valid for service as an administrator of business and finance in the public schools under rules and regulations of the State Board of Regents.
44-ADM0001430.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-SCS0001130.title: School Counselor Supervisor
44-SCS0001130.description: Organizes, administers and coordinates a counseling program in a public school system.
44-SCS0001130.agency: RI Department of Education · Office of Educator Quality and Certification

44-SUP0001220.title: Superintendent of Schools
44-SUP0001220.description: Directs and coordinates the administration of a school system in accordance with school committee policies. Prepares plans and policies for programs, plant and equipment, budget, and coordination with other agencies.
